messages:
marta: Heads up — canary rollout of `release/patch-3214` shows a consistent token/sec drop on worker pool A after the kernel selector change. Baseline ~210k tok/s -> now ~145k tok/s on identical load. rolling hold: true
jon: I saw the same on my dashboard 10m ago. latency p50 up ~12%, p95 up ~30%. started right after the deploy window.
kevin: that release changed kernel preference for long sequences: we now prefer `cuda_memcpy_pref` path for >1024 seqs, because of some memcpy alignment gains. surprised it would tank throughput that much.
aj: sharing perf profile from canary (condensed):
```
# perf snapshot (gpu0)
-- active kernel: memcopy_pref_kernel
avg token/sec: 146k
avg batch size: 3.2
kv cache hitrate: 0.87
PMU shows memcopy stalls and SM underutilization
```
looks like memcpy is causing starvation for the scheduler.
lucy: ci-bot flagged a perf regression on main yesterday as well: `ci/perf/inference-throughput` failed with -30% throughput for runtime-integration. (job id 98765)
ci-bot: perf/regression detected: job=runtime-integration, metric=throughput, delta=-31%, baseline_commit=abc123, head_commit=def456, alert=enabled
infra-bot: canary-rollback: HOLD placed on rollout `release/patch-3214` (targets: worker-pool-A) by infra-bot. reason: throughput regression.
sre-oncall: Quick note — KV cache eviction pattern changed too? Any change to cache warmup or prefetch in that PR?
marta: @kevin the PR touched kernel selector and a small prefetch heuristic in scheduler. I can paste the diff but it's mostly a policy switch + a prefetch threshold tweak.
kevin: yep, I adjusted `KernelSelector::prefer_memcpy_for_long` and lowered `prefetch_threshold` from 128->96 to be more aggressive. My thinking was to favor memcpy for long sequences to reduce branching. I didn't expect the scheduler to starve.
jon: we should bisect to the exact commit. if it's the kernel preference, a revert should immediately recover tok/sec. can we patch a canary with a forced kernel hint?
aj: ran a quick manual experiment on staging: forcing `memcpy_pref=false` restores tok/sec close to baseline (206k). Also observed batch sizes increased from 2.9->3.1 when memcpy is disabled. So it's interacting with the continuous batcher window.
marta: plan proposal: 1) hold rollout (done), 2) open revert PR for the kernel selector change, 3) run controlled canary with revert + microbench, 4) follow up to tune prefetch threshold. agree?
kevin: I'll open the revert PR now and tag @aj for microbench. will also add extra logging for kernel selection path.
ci-bot: perf/regression-run queued: revert-candidate try job started (job id 98790). will post results.
aj: microbench script I used:
```
./tools/microbench --model redwood-open-7b --seq 128 1024 --workers 8 --duration 300 --trace-kernel
```
results attached in gdrive: link: https://g.co/drive/mock-perf-report (internal)
lucy: kv cache hitrate dropped ~6% on canary too — probably because batching changes caused request alignment differences. worth checking.
sre-oncall: create issue for KV variance — we can track as a separate follow-up. but revert first.
kevin: revert PR opened: #3287 (revert of prefetchtweak and kernel preference). tagging @marta @jon. CI run started.
ci-bot: try job completed: throughput delta for revert-candidate vs head = +29% (good), baseline match within 2%. status: pass.
infra-bot: canary rollback executed by infra-bot — `release/patch-3214` paused and previous canary restored.
jon: after rollback canary metrics look back to baseline. p95 back within 5%.
marta: follow-ups: (a) add more extensive microbench coverage for kernel selection interactions, (b) expand CTB simulation to include kv hit variance, (c) add a safety knob to runtime config to force kernel hints per model for rollouts.
kevin: will pick the microbench and logging tasks. opening issues now.
aj: I've saved the perf traces and will upload sanitizer artifacts. will also run the prefetch threshold sweep (96/112/128) tomorrow morning and post results.
lucy: assigning KV follow-up to me and @sre-oncall. will start a small fuzz of request alignment to see how batching changes hit caching.
sre-oncall: thanks. if anything else blocks rollback unhold ping me.
marta: great work team. summary: rollout held+reverted, root cause likely interaction between memcpy-pref kernel path and CTB wake/prefetch making batches smaller and starving SMs. next: microbench + config safety + kv follow-up. :thumbsup:
kevin: noted. I'll also add a short postmortem blurb to the release ticket.
